card.statement:
It is easy to deduce from the proof of Theorem 1.7 that

${}^{L}\mathcal{G}r_{\mathbb{G}_{m}}\simeq\coprod_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}\xi_{n}\qquad\mathcal{G}r^{(2)}_{\mathbb{G}_{m}}\simeq\coprod_{(n,m)\in\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}}\xi_{n,m}$

where the $\xi_{n}$ ’s and the $\xi_{n,m}$ ’s are fat $k$ -points (whose non-reduced ind-scheme structures depend on $n$ , and on $(n,m)$ , respectively). For all the other two-dimensional Grassmannians there is always both a discrete (like above for $\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}$ ) and a continuous part.
This fact, at least, does not prevent a possible Tannakian interpretation of $LJ\mathbb{G}_{m}$ -equivariant sheaves on ${}^{L}\mathcal{G}r_{\mathbb{G}_{m}}$ and of $\mathbb{G}_{m}^{(2)}$ -equivariant sheaves on $\mathcal{G}r^{(2)}_{\mathbb{G}_{m}}$ . We thank S. Raskin for pointing this out.

2. Geometric Grassmannians

Throughout this Section, we fix $X$ a smooth quasi-projective surface over an algebraically closed field $k$ . We denote by $\mathsf{Aff}_{/X}$ the category of affine schemes over $k$ endowed with a map to $X$ , and by $\mathsf{St}_{k}$ (respectively $\mathsf{PreSt}_{k}$ ) the category of fppf stacks in groupoids over $k$ (respectively, the category of pseudo-functors $\mathsf{Aff}^{\mathrm{op}}_{k}\to\mathsf{Grpds}$ , where $\mathsf{Grpds}$ denotes the $2$ -category of groupoids).

2.1. Fiber functors

We will use the formalism of fiber functors, as developed in [9, Section 2.3]. We denote by $\mathcal{F}_{X}$ the forgetful functor $\mathsf{Aff}_{/X}\to\mathsf{St}_{k}$ , which sends $(S\to X)\mapsto S$ . A fiber functor over $X$ is a functor

$\mathcal{F}:\mathsf{Aff}_{/X}\to\mathsf{St}_{k}$

together with a natural transformation $\mathcal{F}\to\mathcal{F}_{X}$ . Actually, all our fiber functors will land inside $\mathsf{Sch}_{k}$ (and, obviously, $\mathcal{F}_{X}$ is indeed a functor $\mathsf{Aff}_{/X}\to\mathsf{Sch}_{k}$ ). Given any stack or scheme $T\to X$ , we denote by $\mathcal{F}_{T}$ the induced fiber functor over $X$ defined via

$\displaystyle\mathcal{F}_{Y}\colon$
$\displaystyle\mathsf{Aff}_{/X}$
$\displaystyle\longrightarrow$
$\displaystyle\mathsf{St}_{k}$

$\displaystyle(S\to X)$
$\displaystyle\longmapsto$
$\displaystyle S\mathbin{\operatorname*{\times}_{X}}T$

We will often write $S/X$ to denote a map $S\to X$ .

paper.title: Two dimensional versions of the affine Grassmannian and their geometric description
paper.abstract: For a smooth affine algebraic group $G$ over an algebraically closed field, we consider several two-variables generalizations of the affine Grassmannian $G(\!(t)\!)/G[\![t]\!]$, given by quotients of the double loop group $G(\!(x)\!)(\!(y)\!)$. We prove that they are representable by ind-schemes if $G$ is solvable. Given a smooth surface $X$ and a flag of subschemes of $X$, we provide a geometric interpretation of the two-variables Grassmannians, in terms of bundles and trivialisation data defined on appropriate loci in $X$, which depend on the flag.
